_**Agent (default)**_

Updated the player overview table logic so rankings are scoped by `team` in addition to `season` and `event/league`.

### What changed

In `app/services/player_service.py`:

- Added a helper `row_team_name()` to extract the current row’s exact `team_name`.
- Extended both ranking helpers to accept optional `team_value`:
  - `league_average_rank(...)`
  - `tournament_final_rank(...)`
- Added team filtering inside each helper:
  - `base = base[team_name == team_value]` (when team is present)
- Passed the row team into rank computation for competition rows:
  - league rank call now includes `comp_team`
  - tournament rank call now includes `comp_team`

### Why this fixes your case

For a player like Alexander Scholz switching from Rottendorf to Rimpar in the same season/event, the rank lookup no longer mixes both teams’ records. Each row’s rank is now computed against the matching team context, so the stats overview table reflects the mid-season team change correctly.

If you want, I can also split the competition rows themselves by `competition + team` (not just the rank filter) so both stints show as separate rows when the same competition appears under two teams.

---

_**Agent (default)**_

Perfect — I’ll adjust the season competition aggregation so rows are grouped by `competition + team`, which will make mid-season team changes show up as separate visible rows in the table.

    function displaySeasonStats(seasons) {
        const tableContainer = document.getElementById('seasonStatsTableContainer');
        if (!seasons || !Array.isArray(seasons) || seasons.length === 0) {
            tableContainer.innerHTML = '<div class="text-center text-muted py-2">No season data available</div>';
            return;
        }

        const tableData = seasons.map(season => ([
            season.season || '-',
            competitionCellHtml(season.season, season.competition, season.is_tournament, season.row_type),
            season.row_type === 'season_total' ? '' : (season.club || '-'),
            season.games || 0,
            (season.total_pins || 0).toLocaleString(),
            season.vs_last_season !== null && season.vs_last_season !== undefined
                ? `${(season.average || 0).toFixed(2)} (${season.vs_last_season > 0 ? '+' : ''}${season.vs_last_season.toFixed(2)})`
                : `${(season.average || 0).toFixed(2)}`,
            season.rank !== null && season.rank !== undefined ? season.rank : '-',
            `<span title="${escapeAttr(`${season.best_game?.date || ''} - ${season.best_game?.event || ''}`)}">${season.best_game?.score || '-'}</span>`,
            `<span title="${escapeAttr(`${season.worst_game?.date || ''} - ${season.worst_game?.event || ''}`)}">${season.worst_game?.score || '-'}</span>`
        ]));

        const tableConfig = {
            data: tableData,
            columns: [
                { title: 'Season' },
                { title: 'Competition' },
                { title: 'Club' },
                { title: 'Games' },
                { title: 'Total Pins' },
                { title: 'Average' },
                { title: 'Rank' },
                { title: 'Best Game' },
                { title: 'Worst Game' }

        if (typeof createTable === 'function') {
            tableContainer.innerHTML = createTable(tableConfig);
        } else {
            tableContainer.innerHTML = '<div class="alert alert-warning">Table creation function not available</div>';
            return;
        }

        const tbodyRows = tableContainer.querySelectorAll('tbody tr');
        seasons.forEach((season, index) => {
            const row = tbodyRows[index];
            if (!row) return;
            if (season.row_type === 'season_total') {
                row.classList.add('table-info', 'fw-bold');
            } else if (season.row_type === 'competition') {
                row.classList.add('table-light');
            }
        });
    }

Great catch — I’ve adjusted the logic to match what you described.

### What I changed

- **Rank is now league-wide (or tournament-wide), not team-internal**
  - Removed team filtering from rank calculations.
  - Rank is computed among all players in that `season + competition`.

- **Competitor count is now included**
  - Backend now computes both:
    - `rank`
    - `competitors` (total ranked players in that competition scope)
  - Table displays it as `rank / competitors` (e.g. `3 / 42`).

- **One league average per competition/season**
  - Competition rows are now grouped by competition only (not competition + team).
  - So Alexander Scholz gets one BayL row/average for the full season (all 45 games), not two separate averages.

### Result for your case

For BayL 25/26:
- Alexander now has a single BayL competition average across both teams combined.
- Rank shows his **league rank** with total competitors, not team-local rank.

If you want, I can also rename the column header from `Rank` to `League Rank` (or `Competition Rank`) to make this explicit in the UI.

Exactly right — the issue was not the catalog entries, but the **translation whitelist returned by `/league/get_translations`**.

I added all `ui.player.*` keys to that exported list in `app/routes/league_routes.py`, so the frontend now actually receives them in `window.translations`.

_**Agent (default)**_

You were right to push on this. I verified the backend now returns the player keys (`/league/get_translations` includes `ui.player.competition` with real values), so the remaining issue was frontend timing/fallback behavior.

### Root cause

- Dynamic player table/chart strings were sometimes rendered before translations finished loading.
- Existing `t(key)` fallback returns the key itself, so you got literals like `ui.player.competition`.

### Fix applied

In `app/templates/player/content.html` I added a robust helper:

- `i18nText(key, fallback)`:
  - prefers `window.translations[key]` when real
  - otherwise uses explicit readable fallback (e.g. `"Competition"`)
  - never leaves raw key placeholders in UI

Then I switched dynamic player strings (table headers, chart labels, messages, placeholders) to use `i18nText(...)`.

So even if translations are late or missing, you now see human labels, not key IDs.

If you still see one specific raw key after this, send me exactly where it appears (header, tooltip, card text) and I’ll patch that exact render path too.

_**Agent (default)**_

Exactly: **structural difference = definition vs exposure vs cache**.

- Existing working keys were:
  1) in i18n catalog,  
  2) in `/league/get_translations` whitelist,  
  3) already present in cached payload.
- New keys were in catalog, then later in whitelist, **but the browser reused stale cached translations** (same version key), so they never reached the page.

### Why your logs prove this

Your warnings show:
- `data-i18n` keys missing from translation payload on page
- dynamic `i18nText(...)` keys also missing
- yet backend itself can have those keys (if queried fresh)

That pattern is classic stale client cache.

### Fix I applied

In `app/templates/base.html`, `loadTranslations()` now validates cached translations against the page’s required `data-i18n` keys:

- if cached map is missing any required key, it logs:
  - `[i18n] Cached translations incomplete for current page; refreshing from server payload`
- then it **replaces cache with fresh server payload** immediately.

So now cache can self-heal when whitelist exposure changes.

If anything still misses, the console now pinpoints whether it’s cache vs payload vs key mismatch.

_**User**_

why wouldnt the backend keys change when we introduce dozens of new labels?

---

_**Agent (default)**_

Great question — you’re thinking correctly.

They **do** change when you add new labels to the i18n catalog.  
But in your case there are **two different “key sets”**:

- `i18n_service._catalog` keys (master backend dictionary)
- `/league/get_translations` whitelist keys (what frontend actually receives)

Your `translations_version` is computed from the **catalog keys only**.

So:

1. When we added `ui.player.*` to `_catalog`, version should change.
2. Later, when we fixed only the **whitelist exposure** in `league_routes.py`, catalog keys did **not** change anymore.
3. Therefore version stayed the same, and cached translations could survive even though frontend payload composition changed.

That’s the structural mismatch: **version tracks dictionary schema, not exposure schema**.

If you want a robust permanent fix, we should compute `translations_version` from both:
- catalog keys
- and the exposed whitelist keys (or just remove whitelist and expose catalog directly).

Implemented.

`/league/get_translations` now includes an **exposure fingerprint** in `translations_version`, so cache invalidates when the endpoint’s exported key list changes.

### What changed

In `app/routes/league_routes.py`:

- Added imports:
  - `hashlib`
  - `inspect`
- In `get_translations()`:
  - Compute `exposure_fingerprint` from the function source
  - Return:
    - `translations_version = <catalog_version>-exp-<fingerprint>`

So now version changes if:
- catalog keys change (old behavior), or
- translation exposure logic/list changes in `get_translations` (new behavior)

This should prevent the exact stale-cache mismatch you hit.

You’re spot on — those are constructor-time false positives.

### What I changed

In `base.html`, I made global missing-key warnings wait until translations are actually loaded:

- Added readiness flag:
  - `translationsReady` + `window.__translationsReady`
- Set it to true only after successful `loadTranslations()` payload application.
- Updated `t(...)` warning condition:
  - warn only when `translationsReady` is true

### Result

- You still get real missing-key warnings.
- Early init calls (before translations are loaded) no longer spam misleading warnings like:
  - `league_standings`
  - `ui.league.aggregation.title`
  - `ui.league.season_overview.title`

So yes — your diagnosis was correct: timing issue, not actual missing translations.

Root cause found and fixed.

You were still seeing `All / latest` because cached translations were considered “fresh” when only a translation **value** changed. Versioning only tracked keys.

### Fix made

In `app/services/i18n_service.py` I changed `translations_version` hashing to include:

- key
- English value
- German value

for each catalog entry.

So when a label text changes (like `ui.tournament.all_latest`), cache version now changes and frontend reloads new strings.

You should now see:

- EN: `Total`
- DE: `Gesamt`

after reload (no manual cache clearing should be needed anymore).

  - Optional tooltip: `Cut at 1234 pins (avg 205.7)`
- **Stage-aware behavior**
  - In `Round Results`, show stage cut line only.
  - In `Leaderboard`, show total cut line at selected stage.
- **Tie handling**
  - If multiple players share cut score, highlight all tied rows the same (don’t force a single row).
- **No layout churn**
  - Keep table columns unchanged; inject via `row_metadata` styling + small label in existing rank cell.

- You already have `row_metadata` + special row styling support.
- It keeps scanability high without widening tables.
- It matches sports standings conventions (zone + threshold line), so users read it instantly.

_**Agent (default)**_

You’re absolutely right, and I’ve reverted the `tables.html` change.

I compared the structures of the two tables:

- `league season standings` (`league_service.py`, `get_league_table_simple`) uses:
  - frozen first group
  - highlighted column group
  - **no row-level background shading** (`row_metadata` is not used there)

- `tournament leaderboard` (`tournament_service.py`, `get_leaderboard_table`) uses:
  - frozen first group
  - **row-level shading via `row_metadata`** with colors like `rgba(44, 160, 44, 0.18)`
  - extra `cell_metadata` on frozen lead columns, but using the same semi-transparent RGBA values

So yes: transparency is being “manipulated” structurally by the table payload itself (semi-transparent RGBA), not just CSS.  
With frozen columns, alpha backgrounds can visually mix with underlying scrolling content and look like bleed/artifacts.

### Structural difference causing this
- League standings: mostly opaque/default surfaces, no shaded rows.
- Tournament leaderboard: shaded rows with alpha (`rgba(..., <1)`), including frozen cells.

### Safe fix path (no library edits)
Only in `tournament_service.py`:
- replace RGBA cutline row colors with opaque colors (hex/rgb without alpha), e.g. 3 solid green tones + solid amber cut row.
- keep everything else unchanged.

If you want, I’ll apply exactly that next, scoped only to tournament leaderboard shading.

### What’s now in place

  - File: `app/templates/tournament/stats.html`

- **Frontend toggle behavior**
  - File: `app/static/js/tournament-stats-app.js`

  - File: `app/routes/tournament_routes.py`

  - File: `app/services/tournament_service.py`

  - Applies `cell_metadata` only to game columns (`G0...G5` / all game columns present)

  - File: `app/static/js/theme/color-utils.js`

    - linearly increases **saturation** across the range
    - interpolates lightness between endpoints

- **Python parity function (backend color lib):**
  - `get_heat_map_color_linear_hue_saturation(...)`
  - File: `app/utils/color_constants.py`
  - Same conceptual behavior so backend-generated cell colors match the new style

- **Round-results heatmap now uses new function:**

- special treatment for `300` and `287` still active

_**Agent (default)**_

Perfect direction — implemented exactly that experiment flow.

### What changed

- Added **heatmap mode buttons** in round results header:
  - `Off`, `Classic`, `Linear HS`, `Sunset`, `Ocean`, `Forest`, `Violet`
  - File: `app/templates/tournament/stats.html`

- Reworked heatmap handling to be **frontend-only dynamic**:
  - No backend refetch/re-render when switching modes
  - Colors are applied directly to existing `G*` Tabulator cells in-place
  - File: `app/static/js/tournament-stats-app.js`

- Fixed the “jump to top” behavior:
  - Mode button clicks now only restyle cells, so page position stays where you are
  - No `renderSection()` call on heatmap-mode click anymore

- Added new color functions in the shared color lib:
  - `getExperimentalHeatMapColor(...)`
  - `getHeatMapColorThreeStopLinear(...)`
  - Existing `getHeatMapColorLinearHueSaturation(...)` still available
  - File: `app/static/js/theme/color-utils.js`

### 5 new gradients (plus classic)

These are exposed via buttons and update live:

- `Linear HS` (your requested linear hue + rising saturation)
- `Sunset`
- `Ocean`
- `Forest`
- `Violet`

### Kept from previous behavior

- Heatmap still only affects `G0..G5` (all `game_*` columns)
- clamp range remains `130..270`
- special handling for `300` and `287` remains

If you want next, I can tune the five presets toward either:
- **maximum contrast/readability** (strongly separates bad vs good), or
- **softer “presentation mode”** (more subtle, less saturated).

---

_**Agent (default)**_

Fixed — the desync came from timing, not state.

### Root cause
When tournament/round changed, the Round Results table was recreated asynchronously.  
The heatmap mode button stayed on `Classic`, but heatmap styling could run **before** `game_*` cells existed, so presentation fell back to plain (looks like `Off`).

### What I changed
In `app/static/js/tournament-stats-app.js`:

- `applyRoundResultsHeatmapToTable()` now returns success/failure.
- Added `scheduleRoundResultsHeatmapApply()` retry helper:
  - retries a few times until round-result cells are actually present
- After rendering round results, we now call the scheduler (instead of single immediate apply).

### Result
- Button state and table presentation now stay in sync across round/tournament changes.
- No more “needs extra click” behavior.
- No scroll jump introduced.

---

### Interval mapping now
- `130–270`: classic heatmap
- `271–299`: dedicated high-band color from theme
- `300`: distinct perfect-game color + border from theme

                entry.append(game_score)
                if enable_heat_map and game_score > 0:
                    col_idx = game_col_index_map[g]
                    if game_score == 300:
                        cell_metadata[f"{row_idx}:{col_idx}"] = {
                            "backgroundColor": get_theme_color("heat_map_perfect") or "#ffc107",
                            "fontWeight": "800",
                            "color": "#111827",
                            "boxShadow": f"inset 0 0 0 2px {get_theme_color('heat_map_perfect_border') or '#b77900'}",
                        }
                    
                    elif 271 <= game_score <= 299:
                        cell_metadata[f"{row_idx}:{col_idx}"] = {
                            "backgroundColor": get_theme_color("heat_map_high_band") or "#ffe7a3",
                            "fontWeight": "600",
                            "color": "#1f2933",
                        }
                    else:
                        cell_metadata[f"{row_idx}:{col_idx}"] = {
                            "backgroundColor": get_heat_map_color(game_score, 130, 270),
                            "color": "#1f2933",
                        }
            entry.append(int(row.get("round_total", 0)))
            entry.append(float(row.get("avg_score", 0.0)))
            entry.append(int(row.get("overall_total", 0)))

Great question — league stats are currently a **hybrid**, but mostly frontend-driven for heatmaps.

- **Frontend-driven heatmap (main path):**
  - In `app/templates/components/tables.html`, `createTableTabulator` computes heatmap ranges from table values when `enableHeatMap` is on, then applies colors with `ColorUtils.getHeatMapColor(...)`.
  - Team-vs-team explicitly enables this in `app/static/js/utils/team-vs-team-utils.js` via `enableHeatMap: true`.

- **Backend provides data context, not full styling (preferred pattern):**
  - `app/services/league_service.py` returns `metadata.score_range` / `metadata.points_range` for team-vs-team, and comments note heatmap is handled frontend-side.
  - That’s very similar to where we just moved tournament round results.

- **Backend still uses some targeted cell styling in league:**
  - Example: diagonal “N/A/self-vs-self” cells use `cell_metadata` with background color from backend.
  - This is not full heatmap logic, just explicit special-case cell markup.

So your proposed architecture matches where league is already headed: backend sends structure/metadata + occasional special markers; frontend does visual interpretation with theme colors.

Yes — good idea.

For your current tournament round-results heatmap, backend-provided ranges are a clean fit if you want flexibility across formats/scoring systems.

- **Why it helps**
  - Keeps business/scoring knowledge server-side
  - Frontend stays purely presentational (uses provided ranges + theme)
  - Avoids hardcoded `130..270` when tournament rules/data change

- **How to do it cleanly**
  - Backend returns metadata in round results payload, e.g.:
    - `metadata.heatmap_ranges.game_score = { min, max, high_band_min, high_band_max, perfect_score }`
  - Frontend reads those values and applies the same style logic you already have.
  - Keep sensible FE fallback defaults if metadata is missing.

- **Important**
  - If your rule is intentionally fixed (always 130..270, 271..299, 300), backend can still provide those constants so FE never hardcodes numbers.

So: **yes, recommended** — as long as backend provides only range metadata, and frontend keeps ownership of color interpretation/styling.

### What I implemented

- **i18n-safe Heatmap toggle text**
  - Added keys:
    - `ui.tournament.heatmap`
    - `ui.common.on`
    - `ui.common.off`
  - Wired them in:
    - `app/services/i18n_service.py`
    - exposed in `app/routes/league_routes.py`
  - Toggle now renders: `Heatmap  [On/Off]` with translated text.

- **Player/deep-link page gets the same heatmap behavior**
  - Applied heatmap styling to `tournamentPlayerRoundTable` (individual tournament results table) too.
  - Same On/Off toggle controls both:
    - main round results table
    - player round table
  - Works for deep links like your `...&player=Alexander+Koller`.

- **Backend provides ranges for both table types**
  - Added identical `metadata.heatmap_ranges.game_score` to:
    - `get_round_results_table` (already there)
    - `get_player_round_table` (now added)
  - Frontend reads these ranges for each table and styles accordingly.

- **Frontend remains sole styling interpreter**
  - No backend per-cell heatmap styling.
  - Backend only provides range metadata + table data.

If you want, next tiny polish can be showing the active numeric range in a tooltip next to the Heatmap toggle (`130–270 | 271–299 | 300`).

You were spot on — it was a visualization clamp, not a data offset.

### Root cause
In the average chart autoscaling, `yMax` was capped at `260`, so any value above 260 (like 261) got clipped to 260 in both line position and tooltip value.

### Fix applied
- `app/static/js/tournament-stats-app.js`
  - changed average chart cap from `260` to `300`.

So 261 now renders and shows correctly in tooltip/value calculations.
